_note: v5 (LoRA on the CLIP image encoder): v4.2's prompt model (learnable crop/disease vectors + symptom descriptions, frozen text encoder) plus trainable LoRA adapters in the last 4 blocks of the image encoder. Why: against the CNN baselines (aniq_baseline_independent_cnn HM 59.7% vs v4.1 52.9%), the CLIP models lose on SEEN pairs (44% vs 55% top-1; seen disease 49% vs 63%) because their image encoder is frozen, while they transfer disease knowledge to unseen crops better (unseen disease at gamma 0: 22-31% vs 13-15%). LoRA lets the image features adapt to leaf lesions with few parameters (393k, vs 86M in the encoder), keeping CLIP's pretrained features and the text side intact. Consequences: image embeddings can no longer be cached, so images are read every epoch (from the 256 px resize cache) with augmentation; that makes each run far slower, so validation uses 1 split instead of v4.2's 3, and max_epochs is 15.
_result: Best model so far, and the first proposed model to beat the CNN baselines. With gamma 0.0725 (validation, epoch 13): harmonic mean 65.1% top-1 / 92.1% top-5 (aniq_baseline_independent_cnn 59.7% / 87.7%; v4.1 52.9% / 87.1%). Seen top-1 53.4% (baseline 54.8%, v4.1 44.2%), unseen top-1 83.2% (baseline 65.5%, v4.1 65.7%). LoRA closed most of the seen gap, as intended: seen disease 57.7% (v4.1 48.9%, baseline 62.5%), seen crop 83.2%; uncalibrated seen top-1 67.1% equals the baseline's 67.2%. The unseen gain comes mainly from better CROP recognition, not better disease transfer: unseen-only diagnostic 86.7% (v4.2 75.6%, baseline 75.8%), unseen crop 86.6% (74.3% uncalibrated, baseline 66.6%), while unseen disease at gamma 0 is 21.1% (v4.1 22.7%, v4 30.9%): adapting the image encoder did not improve, and slightly reduced, disease transfer. Same caveat as before: with 10 unseen pairs over 9 crops, routing an image to the unseen group plus recognising the crop nearly decides the pair (95.4% of unseen images routed to an unseen pair). Calibration transferred better than in v4.1/v4.2: 29.2% of seen-test images go to unseen pairs (v4.1 35.2%), and a diagnostic test sweep (not used for selection) peaks at HM 67.0% near gamma 0.06, close to the chosen 0.0725. Validation: 1 split (seed 42), val HM 51.2% at epoch 13 (v4.1 45.8% on the same split); val HM rose steadily while pseudo-unseen accuracy peaked at epoch 2. Per unseen pair: cherry_aphis_spp 100%, mango_anthracnose 98%, cucumber_downy_mildew 94%, grape_black_rot 87%, cucumber_powdery_mildew 86%, tomato_early_blight 84%, sugarcane_rust 81%, pepper_bell_bacterial_spot 81%, cotton_bacterial_blight 64%, corn_brown_spot 40% (lowest).
title: lora

model._note: Same OpenAI CLIP ViT-B/16 (QuickGELU) as v4.1/v4.2; the text encoder stays frozen.

image_encoder._note: LoRA (dpd/lora.py) on the last 4 of 12 transformer blocks: attention q/k/v and output projections and both MLP layers. Rank 8, alpha 16 (scale 2). B starts at zero, so training starts exactly from pretrained CLIP. Earlier blocks stay frozen and get no gradient. lr 1e-4 (adapters), weight decay 0 like the prompt vectors.

input._note: Images come from the 256 px resize cache (runs/cache/resized_256, shared with the CNN baselines). Test: CLIP's resize 224 + centre crop + CLIP mean/std. The app must standardise uploads the same way (dpd/resize_cache.standardise).

augmentation._note: Same as the CNN baselines except a milder crop scale (0.5-1 instead of 0.25-1), because CLIP's pretrained features expect whole-object views. No hue jitter: colour is diagnostic.

validation._note: Same procedure as v4.2 but 1 split instead of 3: each split is now a full training run with the image encoder in the loop (images instead of cached embeddings). Note v4.2 showed one split can mis-set gamma, so treat v5's gamma with that caveat.

training._note: Prompt vectors as v4.2 (AdamW lr 2e-4, weight decay 0, logit scale 100, loss weights pair 1 / crop 0.5 / disease 0.5). max_epochs 30 -> 15 (v4.1/v4.2 selected epochs 13-18 with cached features; each epoch now re-encodes every image). Batch 256 -> 64 for GPU memory with gradients through 4 image-encoder blocks.

runtime._note: Gradient checkpointing on the text encoder as before. 4 dataloader workers read the resize cache.
